problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ 2x+8y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072159/assets/13df05563b5770bd877481f24da1c69874d73594e6b82230a2159f01367ba030.png)
Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072159/assets/4aff0484efeeb7e39af2bdb169b6fff07ce8ba9348ff3a4839423bf5c9ead97d.png)

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{2} & 2 \\ 4 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{5}{2} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072159/assets/8a7e8b15bc463b00d805547aa64079a1474b5a4595555a5664fba7bfdfb7f62c.png)

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-8$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-8,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
